method: Candidate JSON used only to locate annotation objects. Read primary PDF annotation targets and current source/ledger/assertions; source locators below identify primary physical pages and printed footer pages separately.

features.source: Primary physical p. 71 / printed p. 56; one StrikeOut in §7.5.4 removes the second occurrence of the sentence requiring each cross-reference subsection to contain a contiguous range. The immediately preceding identical sentence remains.
features.verdict: Editorial duplicate deletion; effective requirement remains and no behavior change is required.

features.source: Primary physical pp. 718 and 724 / printed pp. 703 and 709; two StrikeOut/Caret pairs in RichMedia tables correct a citation from Table 315 (3D view) to §13.7.2.3.5 View dictionary.
features.ledger: §13.7.2.3.5 is out-of-scope under the current Clause 13 RichMedia/3D playback exclusion; nearby RichMedia asset extraction is separate.
features.verdict: Cross-reference repair only. It does not add View-dictionary playback or 3D-view interpretation to the admitted consumer scope.
residuals: The current relevant consumers intentionally expose RichMedia assets and refuse playback/appearance derivation; no test of the corrected View dictionary is expected while that scope boundary stands.

features.source: Primary physical p. 40 / printed p. 25; one Caret corrects PARENHESIS to PARENTHESIS in §7.3.4.2.
features.ledger: §7.3.4 string objects; syntax implementation is independent of this prose spelling.
features.verdict: Editorial spelling correction without a changed parser rule.

features.source: Primary physical p. 71 / printed p. 56; two Carets insert non-negative for the subsection-header integers; one StrikeOut deletes NOTE 3's claim that incremental-update subsections can never begin at object number zero.
features.ledger: §7.5.4 Cross-reference table and §7.5.6 Incremental updates, implemented. The current §7.5.4 ledger note and write.rs::incremental_update_freeing rationale still quote the deleted NOTE 3 as the reason object zero cannot be re-headed.
features.verdict: One new test PASS for valid object0 incremental subsection, with detached-free control. Current writer uses a permitted alternate mechanism; its impossibility rationale in code/ledger and ADR0803 cites a deleted note.
residuals: New assertion tests reader acceptance, not general free-list validation or a requirement for the writer to choose reheading.

features.source: Primary physical pp. 22, 23, 70, 73 / printed pp. 7, 8, 55, 58; adds/clarifies cross-reference section and subsection terminology, revises the general table definition to cover information derived from sections, replaces operative §7.5.4 table terminology with section(s), and clarifies Table 15 /Size as one greater than the highest object number across revisions.
features.verdict: Terminology and Size clarification align with section-chain model. Existing tests distinguish section trailers from merged state and test highest stated object number.
residuals: The exact object-zero update subcase is now tested under T91; no additional #149-specific gap identified.

features.source: Primary physical p. 561 / printed p. 546; Table 237 /DigestMethod note removes RSA-only scope and DSA/SHA-1 ignore rule, replacing it with the general rule that where a signing mechanism requires a specific digest, this entry shall be ignored.
features.ledger: §12.7.5.5 signature field seed values; current implementation scope excludes signing-time constraints.
assertions: No dedicated seed-value test was found in current forms_data.rs; existing signature/FieldMDP tests exercise signed transform semantics, not signing-time DigestMethod choice.
features.verdict: Signing-policy clarification does not create an open-time validation or signature-verification requirement. The current ledger explicitly scopes seed values as signing-time constraints and signing is outside this consumer.
residuals: Revisit if a PDF signing consumer is admitted; no signing test drafted.

features.source: Primary physical p. 561 / printed p. 546; Table 237 changes DigestMethod to an unordered array, specifies acceptable values as array items, updates the prose connector, and removes the version qualifier from /V capability 3.
features.ledger: §12.7.5.5 seed-value dictionary. Current ledger identifies DigestMethod as a signing-time constraint; no signer is in admitted scope.
assertions: No current assertion was found for DigestMethod array order/choice; this is outside the absent signing consumer.
features.verdict: The changed choice/order language belongs to signing selection and does not require existing reader open-time behavior. Parsing presence does not assert signing semantics.
residuals: No claim that the parser implements the signing-time preference ordering; that consumer remains absent.

features.source: Primary physical p. 459 / printed p. 444; grouped Issue #162/#288 annotations add a permitted destination dictionary form using /D and optional /SD, with related action-table references.
features.ledger: §12.3.2.4 destinations and related action destination rows.
assertions: crates/pdf-model/src/destination.rs::a_named_destinations_structure_destination_takes_precedence_over_its_page_destination is present in the audit baseline. It checks plain D->page0/Fit, SD->page1/FitH500 via both name/string lookup, and unreadable SD fallback.
features.verdict: Bounded disposition already reviewed by parent in the current crosswalk and destination shard; no duplicate test added.
residuals: The unit fixture uses a StructElem where a full StructTreeRoot would belong; this is model resolver evidence, not full tagged-PDF validity or public host activation. See prior crosswalk parent review.

features.source: Primary physical p. 157 / printed p. 142; informative Table 49 note explains extension URL/revision metadata is encrypted normally and may be meaningless when a consumer does not support the developer's encryption algorithm.
features.ledger: §7.12.3 developer extensions dictionary; generic object-string decryption remains in §7.6 parser scope.
features.verdict: Interoperability note, not an obligation to implement arbitrary extension encryption. It is consistent with generic decryption plus parsed extension fields.
residuals: No custom developer encryption handler is claimed or tested.

features.source: Primary physical p. 553 / printed p. 538; Caret in §12.7.5.2.4 adds that radio-button Off appearance is optional, and if present is named Off in the AP dictionary.
features.ledger: §12.7.5.2.4 is implemented and explicitly claims Off-state handling.
features.verdict: Current AP selection and form tests exercise /Off and named on-state behavior; the erratum's added rule is represented in the current ledger and implementation.
